packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET-14 - unverified blind image reading

Exposure statement: Nothing in my context revealed a proposed identification or earlier reading of this leaf. My standing context mentions that a Fragmentarium/Stams project exists, but gives no reading or identification for this item. I opened only PROMPT.md and the image files (I listed the packet directory, which shows packet.json; I did not open it). No search, editions, or identification attempted. Rubric names (e.g. a sermon attribution) are transcribed because they are written on the leaf, not inferred.

LAYOUT SURVEY (observations)
- Overviews: image-001 = face pencilled "Stams, STA, Frg. 216r"; image-014 = "216v". One leaf, about 21 x 31 cm, reused as a binding wrapper: fold lines along all four edges, cut corners, sewing/tie slits at top, a dark vertical band (former spine turn-in) across the left column on 216r, and a horizontal darkened fold through the middle of 216r. 216r column a is cut away along the left side (line beginnings lost); 216v column b is torn away on the right (line ends lost below line 9).
- Two columns, about 31-33 lines each, ruled. Black text, red rubrics, red initials (one- and two-line; large R, I, C, P on 216v), red cue letters, rubric abbreviations: R(esponsoriu)m (R with stroke), V(ersus) (crossed V), ps, a(n)(tiphona), Invit(atorium), lesson numbers in red (ii, iiii, vi, vij, viij), and red rubric headings ("[D]e spinea corona Cap(itu)l(u)m", "[d]e (com)mentario b(eati) Joh(ann)is ep(iscop)i", "S(er)mo beati B(er)nhardi Abb(at)is .v."). Tentative interpretation: office for a feast (rubric heading names the crown of thorns) with antiphons, psalm cues, responsories and patristic lessons. Small interlinear rubrical notes in black at 216r col a between l4/5 and l8/9, and above 216v col b l25.
- Tiles: 216r: 002 (col a top), 003 (col b top), 004 (col b top right + margin), 005 (col a middle), 006 (col b middle), 007 (col b middle right), 008 (col a lower middle), 009 (col b lower middle), 010 (col b lower right), 011 (col a bottom), 012 (col b bottom), 013 (col b bottom right). 216v: 015 (left margin/col a top-left), 016 (col a top), 017 (col b top), 018 (col a left edge), 019 (col a middle), 020 (col b middle), 021 (col a lower left), 022 (col a lower), 023 (col b lower), 024 (col a bottom-left), 025 (col a bottom), 026 (col b bottom). Overlapping lines counted once; line numbers below are counted from the top of each column (heading = l1), with the main tile named.

Conventions: (..) expansion; "?" after an uncertain reading; [illegible]; [..] lost/unread letters; [red ..] coloured letters.
